Shanghai/Ningbo.waitLabel: SNH 4-7 days · NGB 3-5 days (as of 12 Aug)
Shanghai/Ningbo.note: Terminals at Waigaoqiao, Yangshan and Ningbo-Zhoushan have been open since 10-11 Aug, so this is backlog, not closure. The queue is still not clearing: Linerlytica's newest snapshot is still 16 Aug and shows 1.89m TEU at anchorage with a queue-to-berth ratio of 3.25, by far the worst of the 18 tracked ports. Linerlytica has published nothing new in six days, so those figures are stale rather than improving. Berth-wait figures are still SEKO's 12 Aug numbers (Shanghai 4-7 days, Ningbo 3-5 days) — no source has published newer ones. Kuehne+Nagel's 18 Aug update still reports vessel backlogs, elevated yard utilisation and carriers omitting port calls. Typhoon Saudel's five-day track brings it to roughly 679 km east of the port group, outside the 600 km threat radius but worth watching.
Shanghai/Ningbo.source: SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 12 Aug; Kuehne+Nagel port update, 18 Aug; JMA TC2621, 22 Aug

Haiphong.event: Gulf of Tonkin tropical depression (likely Vietnam Storm No. 4)
Haiphong.note: JMA places the depression about 160 km from the port and moving at roughly 3 km/h, so it is close to stationary. Vietnamese forecasters expect it to strengthen to storm force with Force 8 winds, Force 10 gusts and 2.5-3.5 m seas in the gulf, plus 70-150 mm of further rain across Hai Phong and Quang Ninh. No suspension of container operations has been announced.
Haiphong.source: JMA TC2622 specifications, 22 Aug 00:45 UTC; VietnamNet and VnExpress, 21-22 Aug

Shenzhen (Yantian).event: Gulf of Tonkin tropical depression (likely Vietnam Storm No. 4)
Shenzhen (Yantian).note: Closest forecast approach is about 517 km at +69h, inside the 600 km threat radius but on the far side of the system's slow northward drift. Operations are normal: SEKO reported Shekou and Yantian working to standard ETB-7 gate rules with 2-4 day vessel waits on 12 Aug, and no carrier has issued a closure notice.
Shenzhen (Yantian).source: JMA TC2622 specifications, 22 Aug 00:45 UTC; SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 12 Aug

remarks: Two active systems in the JMA feed. Typhoon Saudel (TC2621) is near the Mariana Islands at 17.9N 146.7E tracking WNW; its closest five-day forecast approach to any tracked port is about 679 km to Shanghai/Ningbo at +120h, so no threat is recorded. Busan, which was on watch last run, is now no fewer than 1035 km from every point on the track — the guidance has shifted west, away from Korea, so the Busan watch is dropped.

The second system, an unnamed tropical depression (TC2622), is sitting in the Gulf of Tonkin about 160 km from Haiphong and barely moving. Vietnam expects it to become Storm No. 4. Slow movement means the main risk is prolonged rain and rough seas rather than a landfall hit.
Linerlytica has published no congestion snapshot since 16 Aug — six days. Every congestion figure on the site is that vintage, including the Shanghai/Ningbo anchorage queue.

Berth-wait figures across the board are stale. SEKO has not updated since 12 Aug and Kuehne+Nagel's next weekly edition is not out. Nothing newer has been published, so no port's reported wait has been changed this run.
No port is currently suspended. MSC has posted no closure advisories.
